CHIEF COMPLAINT
Back pain and right foot tingling

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient reports onset of low back pain and paresthesias in the right foot yesterday while raking leaves in his yard. He initially felt well but symptoms developed approximately two hours after coming inside. He states this is his first significant pain with this activity. He has one prior similar episode approximately three years ago that resolved after one day. He denies regular physical activity. Conservative treatment attempted at home with ice and two doses of ibuprofen provided no relief. Heat therapy via hot shower and sitting both provided some improvement. Pain is present with lumbar flexion but absent with lumbar extension.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Positive for low back tightening and paresthesias in right lower extremity. All other systems reviewed and unremarkable.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Low back pain approximately three years ago, self-limited and resolved after one day.

MEDICATIONS
Ibuprofen, over-the-counter, two tablets taken today without significant relief.

ALLERGIES
Not documented.

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented.

SOCIAL HISTORY
Patient reports minimal regular physical activity. Engages in yard work on an occasional basis.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Back: Tenderness to palpation at L5; pain with flexion; no pain with extension. Lower extremities: Dorsiflexion intact and normal bilaterally; pulses equal in all extremities; paresthesias present in right lower extremity.

RESULTS
X-ray of lumbar spine: Normal, no acute abnormalities.

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
Low back strain. Patient counseled on conservative management. Prescribed meloxicam. Referral to physical therapy for therapeutic exercises, stretching, and reconditioning. Patient advised to rest and modify activity. Follow-up by telephone in two weeks. If symptoms persist, will obtain MRI for further evaluation.
